title: Cómo gestionar un centro de psicología con multiprofesionales
summary: Guía para coordinar agenda, fichas, equipo y facturación de un centro de psicología con multiprofesionales sin perder el control. Ordena tu centro paso a paso.
body_text: Pasar de atender solo a coordinar un equipo de profesionales es un salto enorme. De repente ya no gestionas solo tu agenda, sino la de varias personas. Ya no es tu ficha, son decenas de fichas. Ya no cobras lo tuyo, tienes que ordenar quién factura qué. Gestionar un centro de psicología con multiprofesionales tiene una complejidad que nadie te explica antes de dar el paso. La buena noticia es que con orden y las herramientas correctas, coordinar a un equipo completo puede ser tan manejable como gestionar tu propia consulta. El desafío real de coordinar un equipo en un centro de psicología Cuando un centro de psicología con multiprofesionales crece, la carga administrativa crece con él, pero no de forma proporcional: de forma exponencial. Cada profesional nuevo suma su propia agenda, sus propios horarios, sus propios pacientes y su propia forma de trabajar. Si no hay un sistema que ordene todo eso, terminas con agendas que se pisan, salas ocupadas por dos personas al mismo tiempo, información clínica dispersa y una administración que consume más tiempo del que debería. El error más común es intentar coordinar un centro con las mismas herramientas que servían cuando trabajabas solo: una planilla acá, WhatsApp allá, el calendario del teléfono. Eso funciona para una persona, no para un equipo. Lo que necesita un centro es un sistema donde todo esté conectado. Agenda y espacios: que nadie se pise El primer dolor de cabeza de cualquier centro es la coordinación de agendas y espacios físicos. Cuando varios profesionales comparten salas, el riesgo de sobreagendar un mismo box es constante. La clave está en tener una agenda centralizada que funcione como un todo, no como varias agendas sueltas que alguien tiene que revisar una por una. Idealmente, cada profesional debería tener sus propios servicios y horarios bien definidos, reflejando con exactitud cuándo y qué atiende cada uno , y el sistema debería bloquear automáticamente un espacio cuando ya está ocupado. Ese es justamente el rol de las salas de atención (o box): definir cuántos profesionales pueden atender simultáneamente en cada espacio, de modo que cuando alguien agenda, ese bloque se bloquee para el resto del equipo. Sin llamadas para confirmar quién usa qué sala, sin dobles reservas, sin pacientes esperando en un pasillo porque el box está ocupado. En plataformas como Encuadrado esto se configura una vez y funciona solo desde ahí en adelante. Equipo y permisos: que cada quien vea lo que le corresponde En un centro de psicología con multiprofesionales no todos cumplen la misma función, y no todos deberían ver la misma información. El psicólogo necesita acceder a sus fichas, pero no necesariamente a las finanzas del centro. La persona de recepción necesita gestionar agendas, pero no leer evoluciones clínicas. El administrador necesita verlo todo. Definir roles y permisos claros desde el inicio es una de las decisiones más importantes al armar un centro. Protege la información sensible -especialmente las fichas clínicas, que son materia de confidencialidad- y al mismo tiempo hace que cada integrante trabaje solo en lo que le corresponde, sin ruido ni distracciones. Ordenar el equipo así no es burocracia, es lo que permite que el centro funcione sin que el administrador tenga que estar encima de todo, todo el tiempo. Un buen sistema de gestión te permite asignar a cada persona su propio espacio y nivel de acceso según su función. Servicios y fichas: orden clínico para todo el equipo Un centro con varios profesionales suele ofrecer una variedad amplia de servicios. Si todos conviven en una lista desordenada, tanto el equipo como los pacientes se pierden al momento de agendar. Por eso vale la pena organizar los servicios de forma clara, para que cada profesional tenga su oferta bien definida y los pacientes encuentren fácilmente lo que buscan. En el plano clínico, la regla de oro es que cada profesional gestione sus propias fichas de forma confidencial. Cuando un caso lo requiere, por ejemplo, en equipos que trabajan de forma multidisciplinaria, el acceso compartido a una ficha debería habilitarse de forma controlada y siempre con el consentimiento correspondiente. El control de quién ve qué tiene que ser explícito, nunca al azar. Este es uno de los puntos donde una plataforma diseñada para salud, con fichas certificadas, marca una diferencia real frente a una planilla o un drive compartido. Facturación y finanzas: claridad sobre quién cobra qué Uno de los temas más enredados de gestionar un centro de psicología con múltiples profesionales es el dinero. ¿Los pagos van a una cuenta central o cada profesional recibe lo suyo? ¿Quién emite los documentos tributarios? ¿Cómo se registra quién pagó y quién no? Definir este modelo desde el principio evita descuadres y conversaciones incómodas más adelante. Lo ideal es tener visibilidad clara y en tiempo real del estado de pagos, la ocupación y los ingresos del centro, sin depender de que cada profesional informe manualmente cómo le fue. Esa visibilidad es lo que permite tomar decisiones sobre el centro con información real, no con intuició n. Herramientas como Encuadrado centralizan esta parte y permiten emitir documentos tributarios directamente , pero lo esencial es no dejar las finanzas del centro libradas a la memoria o a planillas dispersas. La cara visible: cómo te ven los pacientes Un centro no es solo su gestión interna: también es cómo lo ven los pacientes desde afuera. Tener una presencia digital donde los consultantes puedan conocer al equipo completo , ver las especialidades disponibles y agendar directamente con el profesional que necesitan es hoy casi imprescindible. Eso no solo mejora la experiencia del paciente: también descarga trabajo de la recepción, porque una parte importante del agendamiento ocurre de forma autónoma, sin llamadas ni mensajes. Crecer sin que la administración crezca al mismo ritmo La gran meta de gestionar bien un centro de psicología con multiprofesionales es esta: poder crecer sin que cada nuevo profesional signifique multiplicar el trabajo administrativo. Cuando la agenda, las salas, los permisos, las fichas y las finanzas están conectadas y ordenadas, sumar un integrante al equipo es simplemente incorporarlo a un sistema que ya funciona. No hay que reinventar procesos ni duplicar esfuerzos. El centro escala con orden. Y eso, al final, es lo que permite que quienes dirigen un centro puedan dedicar su energía a lo que de verdad importa: la calidad de la atención y el bienestar del equipo, no la coordinación interminable de agendas y planillas. ‍

title: Senergy Petroleum: How One President Built It by Merger
summary: Senergy Petroleum made Modern Distribution Management's 2025 Lubricants & Fuels list. Here is how three mergers under one president built it.
body_text: Part of Distributor Playbooks — strategy teardowns of every company on the 2025 MDM Top Distributors lists . Senergy Petroleum turned up on Modern Distribution Management's 2025 Top Distributors list in the Lubricants & Fuels category, one of MDM's 20 annual vertical rankings of North America's largest distributors. The company that made that list did not grow branch by branch. It was assembled, twice, out of family-owned fuel jobbers that had been competing with each other for decades. The more interesting fact is who did the assembling: the same person, for all of it. Two rivals, one merger Senergy Petroleum did not exist before February 2013. Before that date there were two separate Arizona fuel and lubricant jobbers. Brown Evans Distributing, based in Mesa, traced back to 1941 and had passed to Wayne and Kathye Brown, who bought it from the Evans family in 1982. Union Distributing Company, headquartered in Phoenix, was a younger outfit, founded in 1986 by David and Warren Lueth and grown from five employees to 80 over 26 years, according to Jobbers World's coverage of the merger . The two companies served overlapping Arizona territory with overlapping products: wholesale fuel, lubricants, Pacific Pride cardlock sites. Rather than one buying the other, they combined as equals. David Lueth, Warren Lueth, and Kathye Brown retained joint principal ownership of the new entity, and the job of running it went to an outsider: Chris Lindblom, previously president of Canyon State Oil. That hire is the detail worth sitting with. Lindblom did not inherit a family business. He was brought in specifically to run a merger between two families that had just agreed to stop competing, and by the account in Jobbers World he framed the deal as a bet on consolidation accelerating across the fuel jobber industry, not a one-off convenience. The same operator, twice more He was right about the consolidation, and he stayed at the wheel for it. In April 2020, Senergy combined with Honstein Oil, a Southwest heritage distributor Senergy itself describes as carrying more than four decades of operating history into the deal. That merger is also where the "history dating to 1941" line on Senergy's own site comes from: it is not Senergy's founding date, it is the lineage of the oldest predecessor company folded into it. The combined firm crossed 300 employees and picked up certifications as a Chevron First Source marketer and a Phillips 66 Top Tier Lubricants marketer, meaning it sells and services more than one major's branded lubricant line rather than tying itself to a single refiner relationship. Then, effective November 3, 2022, Senergy acquired Hill Petroleum , a Colorado distributor operating out of Arvada and Greeley, pushing the combined company past 500 employees and adding Colorado density on top of the existing Arizona, New Mexico, Nevada, Texas, Utah, and Wyoming footprint. Every one of these deals was announced with the same message to customers: same account manager, same pricing, same contract terms, only the name on the invoice changes. That is not boilerplate. It is the operating thesis repeated three times. The insight: continuity is the moat Most fuel and lubricant distribution roll-ups follow a familiar pattern in this vertical: a financial sponsor buys a founder out, installs professional management, and integrates the acquisition into a platform built for eventual resale. Senergy's public record shows something different. The founding principals from the 2013 merger, the Lueths and the Browns, retained ownership rather than cashing out to a sponsor, and the president who closed that first deal has been the one closing every deal since. There is no visible private-equity platform behind Senergy's name, and the leadership has not turned over across three combinations spanning more than a decade. That continuity is the unique thing about how this company got here. A roll-up usually trades founder relationships for scale, and customers feel the seams: new account reps, renegotiated terms, a different logo on the truck. Senergy's version kept the same operator quarterbacking the assembly and kept telling acquired customers, credibly, that nothing about their day-to-day relationship would change. Whether that holds as the company adds a fourth or fifth predecessor company is the real test of the model, since the promise gets harder to keep the more territories and cultures get stitched together. So far, across Arizona, Colorado, and the rest of the Rockies and Southwest, it has held long enough to put the combined company on MDM's list under one name. What the footprint bought The result is a distributor with 15 cardlock fueling locations across Arizona, New Mexico, Texas, Oklahoma, and Colorado, according to Senergy's own site , plus bulk fuel delivery, lubricants, diesel exhaust fluid, and chemical supply lines layered on top through each acquisition. Union Distributing brought cardlock infrastructure. Brown Evans brought its Pacific Pride network and Mesa base. Honstein brought scale and additional Rockies territory. Hill brought Colorado. None of that reads as organic growth. It reads as a company that figured out, in 2013, that the fastest way to build regional density in fuel and lubricant wholesaling was to stop competing with the neighbors and start buying them, carefully, with the same person managing every handoff. Distribution rewards the unglamorous work of keeping a catalog current, a fleet running, and a customer's account intact through every change of ownership behind it. Senergy Petroleum's run is one version of what it takes to do that at regional scale without losing the relationships that got it there.

title: Amazon EC2 now surfaces the public SSM parameters associated with public AMIs
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon EC2 now surfaces the public SSM parameters associated with public AMIs
body_text: Amazon EC2 now surfaces the AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Parameter Store parameters associated with public AMIs directly in the AMI metadata. When you describe a public AMI, the response includes the associated public SSM parameter, making it easy to discover and reference in your configurations. Previously, finding the SSM parameter associated with a public AMI required searching through SSM parameter namespaces manually. Now, when you describe a public AMI, the response includes the public SSM parameter it is associated with. This allows you to discover the SSM parameter for a public AMI easily and use it as an alias that always resolves to the latest version, simplifying AMI updates across your infrastructure. This capability is available to all customers at no additional cost in all AWS regions including AWS China (Beijing) Region, operated by Sinnet, and AWS China (Ningxia) Region, operated by NWCD, and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, please visit the documentation .

title: How to Identify and Treat Common Fungal Infections
summary: Struggling with stubborn itching, ringworm, or nail fungus? Explore symptoms and targeted antifungal treatments to clear infections safely and effectively.
body_text: Skin Fungal Infections Scalp & Hair Fungal Infections Fungal Nail Infections FAQs Unbearable itching, sudden red rings, flaky scalps, or stubborn yellowed nails; fungal infections have a habit of showing up uninvited and making life deeply uncomfortable. But the good news here is that they’re treatable when matched with the right care. Fungal infections are of several types including athlete’s foot and ringworm, and depending on their types the treatment often changes. In this complete guide, we’ll break down the most common fungal skin, scalp, and nail infections, their symptoms, and find out the dermatologists-recommended treatment plan ensuring effective results. Skin Fungal Infections: Symptoms & Treatments Your skin is constantly in contact with fungi, but problems start when warm, humid environments allow them to multiply out of control. Skin fungal infections often look similar (red, itchy, and irritated) which makes identifying the exact type crucial for picking the right remedy. Let’s have a look at the four most common skin fungal infections, how to spot them, and the specific targeted treatments that eliminate them. 1. Body Ringworm (Tinea Corporis) Despite its name, ringworm has nothing to do with worms. It is a surface fungal infection caused by dermatophytes that feed on keratin in the skin. Symptoms: Circular, ring-like red patches with slightly raised, scaly borders. Clear or less inflamed skin in the center of the ring. Intense itching and mild burning sensations. Patches that slowly expand outward on the chest, back, arms, or legs. Targeted Treatments: Topical antifungal creams are the first line of defense for body ringworm. They penetrate the top layer of the skin to stop fungal cell growth. Lulifin Cream & Lulican Cream (Luliconazole): Highly potent broad-spectrum topical antifungals that offer fast relief from itching and require short treatment durations. Ebernet Cream (Eberconazole): Excellent for inflammatory fungal infections, reducing both the fungus and skin irritation. Onabet Cream (Sertaconazole): It provides a dual action; killing the fungus while offering strong anti-inflammatory properties to calm red, irritated skin. 2. Jock Itch (Tinea Cruris) Jock itch is a fungal infection that thrives in warm, moist areas of the body, most commonly affecting the groin, inner thighs, and buttocks. It is especially common in athletes or anyone who sweats heavily. Symptoms: Persistent, intense itching and redness in the groin folds. A well-defined border that may feel scaly or have tiny bumps. Flaking, peeling, or cracking skin in the inner thigh region. Worsening discomfort during exercise, walking, or hot weather. Targeted Treatments: Treatment for jock itch requires a two-step approach: soothing the inflamed skin and keeping the area dry to prevent the fungus from spreading. Soothing Creams: Apply creams like Luly Cream or Sertagold Cream to eliminate the underlying fungus while relieving friction-induced soreness. Absorbent Antifungal Powders: Use dusting powders like Abzorb Dusting Powder or Candid Dusting Powder (Clotrimazole) after showering. These absorb sweat, eliminate moisture pockets, and provide active antifungal protection throughout the day. 3. Athlete’s Foot (Tinea Pedis) Athlete’s foot targets the damp environments of the feet; specifically between the toes and on the soles. It spreads easily in shared humid spaces like gym locker rooms, public showers, and swimming pools. Symptoms: Itching, burning, or stinging between the toes or on the soles of the feet. White, soggy, or peeling skin between the smallest toes. Dry, scaly, or thick skin on the heels and sides of the feet. Occasional blistering or painful skin cracks (fissures). Targeted Treatments: Foot infections require active ingredients that can penetrate tough skin while managing sweat buildup inside footwear. Topical Solutions & Creams: Onabet-SD 30 Topical Solution provides deep penetration in hard-to-reach crevices between toes without leaving greasy residue. Antifungal Powders: Dust Candid Dusting Powder or Abzorb Dusting Powder directly inside socks and shoes daily to neutralize trapped fungi and control sweat. 4. Tinea Versicolor (Pityriasis Versicolor) Unlike ringworm, Tinea Versicolor is caused by an overgrowth of Malassezia, a yeast naturally present on human skin. When exposed to heat, humidity, or excessive oil, this yeast multiplies and interferes with normal skin pigmentation. Symptoms: Uneven patches of discolored skin on the chest, back, neck, or upper arms. Patches that appear lighter (hypopigmented) or darker (hyperpigmented) than your natural skin tone. Dry, fine scaling over the affected patches. Patches that become more noticeable after sun exposure (as the affected areas fail to tan). Targeted Treatments: Because Tinea Versicolor often covers larger body areas like the chest and back, liquid washes, suspensions, and medicated shampoos are the easiest and most effective applications. Candid TV Suspension (Clotrimazole + Selenium Sulfide): Works by slowing down yeast growth while exfoliating away the flaky, discolored skin layers. Saldan TVC Lotion : Designed specifically to treat widespread yeast overgrowth across the torso. Ketostar Anti-Dandruff Shampoo / Wash (Ketoconazole): Can be lathered over the affected body parts during a shower, left on for 3–5 minutes, and rinsed off to systematically lower skin yeast levels. Scalp & Hair Fungal Infections Fungal infections on the scalp are not only uncomfortable, but if left untreated, they can lead to temporary hair loss, severe scaling, and persistent inflammation. The scalp's natural oils and hair follicles provide an ideal environment for fungi and yeasts to thrive when balance is disrupted. Here is how to spot the two most common scalp fungal issues and the targeted treatments that clear them up. 1. Scalp Ringworm (Tinea Capitis) Scalp ringworm is a fungal infection of the scalp skin and hair shafts caused by dermatophytes. It is highly contagious and commonly affects children, though adults can contract it too. Symptoms: Circular, scaly, or bald patches on the scalp where hair has broken off at or just above the surface. Small black dots scattered across the scalp (from broken hair shafts). Severe itching, redness, and tender, swollen areas. In severe cases, soft, raised, pus-filled swellings called kerions. Targeted Treatments: Scalp fungal infections require medicated shampoos to clear fungal spores, clean hair follicles, and prevent the infection from spreading across the head. Xampu-KZ Shampoo (Ketoconazole): A powerful broad-spectrum antifungal shampoo that stops fungal cell membrane synthesis, clearing spores directly at the root. Ketonext CT Shampoo (Ketoconazole + Coal Tar): Combines antifungal action with coal tar to simultaneously kill the fungus, reduce scalp flaking, and soothe intense itchiness. C Win Shampoo & Anaboom AD Anti-Dandruff Shampoo : Specialized medicated hair washes that cleanse the hair shaft, reduce surface fungal load, and soothe inflamed scalp skin. 2. Severe Dandruff & Seborrheic Dermatitis Unlike ringworm, severe dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis are caused by an overreaction to Malassezia, a yeast naturally present on oily areas of the scalp. When sebum production surges or skin immunity dips, this yeast triggers rapid skin cell shedding and severe inflammation. Symptoms: Thick, greasy, white or yellowish scales and crusts stuck to the scalp and hair shafts. Patches of red, inflamed skin that may extend to the hairline, eyebrows, or behind the ears. Persistent, frustrating itching and scalp tightness. Fine, dry flaking that falls onto shoulders. Targeted Treatments: Effectively controlling seborrheic dermatitis requires a combination of antifungal agents to suppress yeast growth and keratolytics to dissolve stubborn, greasy buildup. Kz Plus Lotion / Shampoo (Ketoconazole + Zinc Pyrithione - ZPT): A gold-standard dual-action treatment. Ketoconazole destroys the yeast, while Zinc Pyrithione regulates oil production and stops flaking. Tarscalp Shampoo (Coal Tar + Salicylic Acid / Ketoconazole blends): Uses coal tar to slow down rapid skin cell turnover and salicylic acid/coal tar combinations to break down thick, crusty scale buildup on the scalp. Bioderma Nodé DS+ Anti-Dandruff Shampoo : A dermatological formula designed for persistent dandruff; it regulates sebum, calms severe itching, and prevents recurrent yeast flare-ups without stripping natural hair moisture. Fungal Nail Infections (Onychomycosis) Fungal nail infections, medically known as onychomycosis, occur when fungi, usually dermatophytes, yeasts, or molds, enter through tiny cracks in the nail or surrounding skin. Because nails are thick and grow slowly, nail fungus is notoriously stubborn and requires specialized, deep-penetrating treatments to reach the infected nail bed. Toenail & Fingernail Fungus While nail fungus can affect both hands and feet, toenails are far more vulnerable due to the dark, moist environment inside shoes and reduced blood flow to the toes. Symptoms: Discoloration: Nails turn whitish, yellow, or dark brownish-black. Thickening & Distortion: The nail plate becomes abnormally thick, distorted in shape, or difficult to trim. Brittleness: Edges become fragile, crumbly, or ragged, often breaking off easily. Debris Buildup: Dark, chalky debris collects beneath the nail, raising it off the skin (onycholysis). Foul Odor or Discomfort: A faint unpleasant odor or pain when pressure is applied (such as when wearing tight shoes). Targeted Treatments: Standard creams often fail to treat nail fungus because they cannot penetrate the hard keratin surface of the nail. Medicated nail lacquers act like a waterproof coating that locks the active antifungal agent onto the nail, allowing it to penetrate deep down over time. Loceryl Nail Lacquer (Amorolfine 5%): A gold-standard topical lacquer that forms a durable, antifungal film over the nail. It penetrates the nail plate to destroy fungal cell membranes and typically requires application only once or twice a week. Amrolstar Nail Lacquer (Amorolfine): Provides high-strength Amorolfine to effectively treat mild-to-moderate fungal nail infections and stop the infection from spreading to adjacent nails. Fungicros Nail Lacquer (Amorolfine): Specially formulated to adhere to thick toenail surfaces, continually delivering active medication to the underlying infected nail bed. Nailon Nail Lacquer : An effective daily or weekly targeted lacquer designed to strengthen fragile nail structure while clearing persistent fungal spores. Candidiasis & Yeast Infections Yeast infections are caused primarily by Candida species; most commonly Candida albicans. Unlike dermatophytes that thrive strictly on dead keratin (like outer skin layers, hair, and nails), Candida is an opportunistic organism that normally lives in small amounts on human skin and mucosal membranes. When environmental conditions change; such as increased heat, moisture, friction, or altered skin immunity, it multiplies rapidly, leading to distinct surface infections. Here is how to spot cutaneous yeast infections and oral thrush, along with the targeted treatments used to manage them. Cutaneous (Skin Fold) Yeast Infections Cutaneous candidiasis, frequently appearing as Intertrigo, targets warm, moist pockets of the body where skin rubs against skin. Common areas include under the breasts, in groin creases, around the armpits, and inside deep abdominal skin folds. Symptoms: Bright Red Patches: Raw, shiny, beefy-red skin in skin folds. Satellite Lesions: Small, distinct red dots or tiny pus-filled bumps scattered just outside the main edge of the rash. Maceration & Cracking: Soft, whitish, waterlogged skin that easily cracks, stings, and oozes. Intense Burning & Itching: Friction makes the area extremely tender, sore, and itchy. Targeted Treatments: Clearing skin fold yeast requires a combination of antifungal agents to stop yeast overgrowth and absorbent products to reduce moisture accumulation and friction. Eberfine Cream (Eberconazole) & Lulizol Cream (Luliconazole): Broad-spectrum topical antifungals that penetrate raw skin layers to stop yeast cell synthesis while reducing localized inflammation. Candid Dusting Powder (Clotrimazole): Essential for fold management. Applying this powder daily keeps skin folds dry, prevents sweat accumulation, and reduces friction between skin surfaces. Oral Thrush (Oropharyngeal Candidiasis) Oral thrush is a fungal infection of the mucous membranes inside the mouth and throat. It is most common in infants, denture wearers, individuals using inhaled corticosteroids, or those with lowered immune systems. Symptoms: White Lesions: Creamy, white, curd-like patches on the tongue, inner cheeks, roof of the mouth, or gums. Bleeding when Scraped: White patches that leave red, raw, and slightly bleeding tissue when gently wiped or scraped away. Soreness & Swallowing Difficulty: Redness, burning, or pain inside the mouth that makes eating or swallowing uncomfortable. Corner Cracking (Angular Cheilitis): Redness, flaking, and painful cracking at the outer corners of the mouth. Targeted Treatments: Because the mouth is a moist mucosal environment, oral thrush is managed with specialized oral formulations (suspensions, lozenges, or paints) designed to coat the interior lining of the mouth directly. Candid Mouth Paint (Clotrimazole 1%): Specially formulated liquid suspension that adheres to the inner lining of the cheeks, tongue, and gums. It continuously releases active Clotrimazole into the saliva to destroy yeast cell walls and clear white lesions. Clotrimazole Troches / Lozenges (10 mg) : Slowly dissolve in the mouth over 15 to 30 minutes, delivering targeted antifungal medication directly to the oral mucosa. Application Tip for Oral Suspensions/Paints: Apply after meals or drinks. Avoid eating or drinking for at least 30 minutes after applying oral antifungal washes or paints to give the medication sufficient time to bind to mucosal tissue and act effectively. Choosing the Right Anti-Fungal Format Antifungal medications come in several distinct delivery formats, such as creams, dusting powders, medicated soaps, and oral tablets. Choosing the right format depends heavily on the infection’s location, severity, and skin environment. 1. Topical Antifungal Creams & Lotions Best For: Spot treatment of localized skin infections (e.g., body ringworm, mild jock itch, tinea versicolor patches). How They Work: Emulsions and lotions penetrate the outer layers of skin (stratum corneum) to deliver concentrated active ingredients directly to the active fungus site. When to Choose: Select creams when dealing with dry, scaly, or inflamed patches that need moisture along with antifungal action. Lotions are preferred for broader skin areas (such as the back or chest) because they spread easily without leaving a greasy residue. Top Examples: Lulifin Cream, Ebernet Cream, Onabet Cream, Sertagold Cream. 2. Antifungal Dusting Powders Best For: Sweaty, moisture-prone body folds (e.g., groin, underarms, beneath breasts, and between toes). How They Work: Dusting powders provide a dual-action mechanism. The active antifungal agent eliminates fungal cells, while the absorbent powder base (such as talc or starch) absorbs excess sweat and reduces friction between skin folds. When to Choose: Ideal during summer months, after workouts, or alongside creams to keep high-sweat areas dry and prevent infection recurrence. Top Examples: Abzorb Dusting Powder, Candid Dusting Powder, Candisweat Dusting Powder . 3. Medicated Antifungal Soaps & Body Washes Best For: Broad skin hygiene, controlling yeast overgrowth, and supporting active topical treatments. How They Work: Formulated with broad-spectrum antifungals like Ketoconazole, these bars and body washes reduce the overall fungal load on the skin's surface during daily bathing. Lathering and leaving the product on the skin for 3 to 5 minutes allows the active ingredient to penetrate the skin barrier effectively. When to Choose: Use medicated soaps as a primary body wash for widespread conditions like Tinea Versicolor or as an ongoing preventive step for individuals prone to frequent fungal infections. Top Examples: Ketostar Medicated Soap , Kz Plus Medicated Soap , Konaz 2% Soap , Belzole Soap . 4. Oral Antifungal Tablets & Capsules Best For: Severe, extensive, recurrent, or deep-seated fungal infections (e.g., fungal nail infections, widespread body ringworm, or scalp infections). How They Work: Oral antifungals work systemically. Once ingested, the active drug circulates through the bloodstream to reach tissues that topical treatments cannot easily penetrate, such as infected nail beds and hair follicles. When to Choose: Recommended when topical creams fail to clear the infection, when the infection covers large surface areas, or when treating hard keratinized tissues like thick toenails. ( Note: Oral antifungals require a doctor's prescription). Top Examples: Canditral SB Capsules , Itracot Capsules , Itragreat Capsules, Zimig 250mg Tablets . Quick Comparison Matrix Format Key Function Ideal Skin Area Primary Benefit Creams & Lotions Direct, localized treatment Arms, legs, torso, face Deep penetration & moisture balance Dusting Powders Moisture absorption & fungal control Groin, underarms, feet, skin folds Keeps skin dry & stops friction Medicated Soaps Surface hygiene & yeast reduction Whole body, scalp margins Easy wash-off application for large areas Oral Tablets Systemic internal treatment Nails, hair follicles, severe skin areas Reaches deep-seated infections via blood flow Final Thought: Seeking Medical Advice Before Trying Home Remedies While natural DIY remedies like tea tree oil, apple cider vinegar, or garlic pastes are often touted for skin issues, attempting to treat a fungal infection with home remedies can do more harm than good. Many skin conditions; such as eczema, psoriasis, or bacterial infections closely mimic fungal rashes, and thus, it’s important to understand the fungal infections effectively. Misdiagnosing them can lead to applying harsh, undiluted ingredients that cause severe skin irritation, chemical burns, or secondary contact dermatitis. Furthermore, home remedies lack the standardized potency required to penetrate deep into skin layers, hair follicles, or nail beds; partial or ineffective treatment allows fungal spores to survive, adapt, and return as chronic, resistant infections. A brief consultation with a dermatologist ensures an accurate diagnosis and a safe, clinically proven targeted treatment plan that clears the infection effectively.

title: Digital Signature Essential Rules
summary: Learn the essential digital signature rules to ensure professionalism and security in your digital transactions. Discover expert tips on signing documents online with the Kaagaz App.
body_text: Why Digital Signature Etiquette Matters In the modern digital landscape, electronic signatures have become an essential part of business and personal transactions. A digital signature is legally binding, convenient, and enhances efficiency. However, following proper digital signature etiquette is crucial to maintaining professionalism and security. Whether you're using the Kaagaz App or any other platform, understanding the best practices for signing documents electronically helps prevent security risks and legal issues. Key Etiquette Rules for Digital Signatures Always Use Your Legal Name Using your legal name in digital signatures ensures authenticity and professionalism. Avoid nicknames or informal variations to prevent complications in official documents. Review Documents Carefully Before Signing Before applying your e-signature , review the document thoroughly. Ensure accuracy and check for blank spaces that could be altered post-signature. This simple step can help you avoid errors and potential fraud. Use a Secure Platform for Signing A secure signing platform is crucial for safeguarding your documents and electronic signature. The Kaagaz App offers encryption to ensure your digital signature remains protected from unauthorized access. To further enhance security, you may want to add or remove a PDF lock to prevent unauthorized modifications after signing. How to Digitally Sign Your Document Using Kaagaz App Step 1: Download the Kaagaz App Install the Kaagaz App from the Google Play Store or App Store . Step 2: Access the E-Sign Feature Open the app, navigate to the ‘E-Sign’ button, or select the ‘Edit PDF’ tab and choose the ‘E-Sign’ option. Step 3: Upload or Capture Your Document Upload an existing document or take a picture using the app’s scanner. Step 4: Create and Customize Your Signature Use the digital signature tool to sign the document. You can adjust opacity, color, and size to personalize your signature. Step 5: Place and Save Your Signature Position your electronic signature on the document and save it securely. The Kaagaz App automatically stores your recent signatures for easy access. For more advanced document edits, you may find our How to Edit a PDF guide useful. Common Mistakes to Avoid When Using Digital Signatures Signing Without Understanding the Document Never sign a document without fully understanding its contents. Read the terms and ensure you agree with all clauses before signing. Ignoring Document Alterations Post-Signature Some platforms notify users of alterations after signing, but it’s always best to double-check manually. Look for any unauthorized edits before submitting your signed document. Using Weak Passwords When signing documents digitally, use a strong password to protect your files. Avoid easily guessed passwords and enable multi-factor authentication when available. Failing to Back Up Important Documents Always store a backup of your digitally signed documents in a secure location. The Kaagaz App offers a cloud-based system for safe storage and retrieval. Not Verifying the Recipient's Compatibility Before sending a digitally signed document, verify that the recipient’s platform is compatible with your digital signature software. This ensures smooth access and verification of the document. Conclusion Adhering to digital signature etiquette enhances security, professionalism, and efficiency in online document transactions. By following these best practices and using a trusted tool like the Kaagaz App , you can ensure your digital transactions remain legally sound and secure . For additional PDF management needs, check out our guides on merging and splitting PDFs and compressing PDFs to optimize your document workflow. By staying informed and leveraging the right tools, you can seamlessly integrate digital signatures into your daily processes while keeping your documents safe and professional.

title: How Affidavits Work and When to Use One | ROGER Blog
summary: Learn what an affidavit is, when you need one, and how to create and sign it, electronically or in person. Understand its legal role in family law, probate, and more.
body_text: ❓What is an affidavit? An affidavit is a written statement of facts that you swear to be true, usually in front of a notary or authorized witness. It’s used in legal settings where someone needs to formally confirm the truthfulness of information, like in court cases, estate matters, or official declarations. Once signed and witnessed, it becomes a legally binding document. Lying in an affidavit can lead to penalties, including perjury charges. If you’re signing one, make sure everything in the document is accurate and honest. ❓Do affidavits need to be notarized? Yes, in most cases affidavits must be notarized or signed in front of someone authorized to witness legal documents. This adds a layer of authenticity and ensures that the statement was made voluntarily and with an understanding of the legal consequences. Depending on where you are, this witness could be a notary public, lawyer, or court official. Online notarization is becoming more common, making the process even more accessible. ❓Is an affidavit the same as a sworn statement? They’re similar, but not always the same. Both involve stating facts under oath, but an affidavit is typically a more formal document that’s signed and witnessed as part of a legal process. A sworn statement may or may not require a notary, depending on the jurisdiction or the purpose. If you're not sure which one applies to your situation, it's best to check with your lawyer or the institution requesting the document. ❓When would you use an affidavit? You might need an affidavit in a variety of situations. These can include confirming your identity, verifying residency, stating income or assets, or providing testimony in a legal dispute. They're commonly used in family law, probate matters, immigration cases, and even for routine paperwork like name changes. Whether you're in court or simply completing a legal process, affidavits allow you to present verified facts without needing to appear in person. ❓Can you create and sign affidavits electronically? Yes, in many regions you can now create, sign, and notarize affidavits electronically. Platforms like ROGER make it possible to prepare your affidavit, sign it digitally , and even have it notarized remotely using secure video verification. However, legal requirements can vary by state or country. Before proceeding with an e-signature or remote notarization, check that it’s accepted by the court or organization requesting the document. ❓What should be included in an affidavit? An affidavit should clearly include your full name, address, and a statement that you are swearing the contents are true. Then comes the main body, where you list the facts you’re declaring. Finally, it should include your signature, the date, and space for notarization or witnessing. Keep the language factual and straightforward. Avoid speculation or opinions. If you're unsure how to format one, there are templates available, or you can consult a legal professional. ❓Is an affidavit legally binding? Yes, once properly signed and witnessed, an affidavit is a legally binding document. It’s considered evidence in legal proceedings and holds the same weight as in-person testimony. If it’s proven that you knowingly lied in an affidavit, you could face perjury charges, fines, or even jail time. Because of its legal weight, you should never sign an affidavit unless you're confident everything in it is true to the best of your knowledge. ❓How long is an affidavit valid? Affidavits do not typically expire, but their relevance can depend on the context. For instance, if you swore an affidavit to confirm your income or residency, it might only be considered accurate for a limited time, such as 30 or 60 days, depending on who’s requesting it. Courts and agencies usually assess affidavits based on when they were signed and whether the information remains current. So even though your affidavit is legally valid, make sure it's still factually accurate if you're reusing it. 📝 Looking for more contract tips? title: SOLV Energy | Skip the Grid 2026: Celebrating 5 Years of Powering…
summary: We are the leading EPC contractor and O&M provider in the U.S, delivering solar solutions that generate good energy for people and the planet.
body_text: Powering as One Team From Red Mesa to Chinle to Holbrook, SOLV Energy and our partners have spent five years proving that the solar industry can show up for the people closest to the energy gap—not just once, but year after year. Within the Navajo Nation sits half of the Holbrook Unified School District (HUSD), where nearly two-thirds of students are Native American. A significant number of those students go home each night to a house without a reliable source of electricity, in the second poorest county in the United States. This year's trip was the largest in Skip the Grid history, powering 50 homes across Holbrook, Arizona, extending into the Hopi Reservation, with more than 90 students impacted across HUSD. Since the initiative launched five years ago, more than 200 homes now live with electricity—each one representing a family that can now refrigerate medication, study after dark, and start the day on their own terms. The 25 Cal Poly SLO students and faculty who made the trip this year had spent an entire quarter preparing before a single panel went up—developing installation plans, coordinating Goal Zero systems, and accounting for the unique roof angles and demands of each home. When installation began, students served as team leads on the initiative that took place during what was meant to be their Spring Break. "Skip the Grid is known as an interdisciplinary project here at Cal Poly SLO—being able to represent all seven colleges is a one-of-a-kind experience," said Sean Murphy, a Mechanical Engineering student and third-time Skip the Grid participant. "The first time I attended, we powered 20 homes. Now we provided electricity to 50 homes in three days—and I think that's incredible." Heart of America had been doing their own groundwork long before our boots hit the ground—building relationships with the Holbrook Unified School District, identifying families without access to power, and earning the community trust that makes the work possible in the first place. Their presence is what turns an installation trip into something lasting. Nextpower also joined as a key collaborator, sending their own employees to work alongside SOLV Energy teams in the reservation—a signal that Skip the Grid has grown beyond a single company's initiative into something the broader energy industry wants to be part of.

title: How Bad Is 0.22? Putting PE CEO Selection Accuracy in Context
summary: The market knowledge your talent decisions depend on — centralized. Verata unifies company intelligence, executive data, and search management in one platform built for PE talent and executive search.
body_text: The most common pushback we hear is that 0.22 represents the floor, not the ceiling -- that experienced search consultants and operating partners bring judgment, pattern recognition, and reference-based insights that a model cannot capture. This is a reasonable hypothesis, and it may even be true. But it shifts the burden of proof in an important direction. If the value of executive search lies in factors that are not captured by observable career characteristics, then the industry should stop selling those characteristics as the basis for candidate selection. The typical search spec -- prior CEO title required, top MBA preferred, 15+ years in vertical -- is a credential filter. If credentials do not predict outcomes, then the credential filter is not adding value. Whatever the search consultant brings beyond the filter may matter, but the filter itself is demonstrably noise. More importantly, the 0.22 figure represents the best case for credential-based prediction. We gave the model every advantage: a large dataset, multiple architectures, extensive feature engineering. If there were a strong signal hiding in the resume, we would have found it. The signal exists somewhere -- some CEOs genuinely do outperform others -- but the resume does not contain it. This is actually good news. It means the search for better prediction should focus on what resumes cannot capture, not on more sophisticated ways to read them.

title: Open Source: Healthcare's Structural Data Advantage
summary: Open source gives healthcare interoperability platforms a structural trust advantage. By making patient-matching logic and other decisions publicly reviewable, organizations can verify how critical decisions are made instead of relying on vendor claims.
body_text: Every healthcare interoperability platform makes judgment calls about a patient’s identity. When a record comes in for “Robert Smith,” born March 12, 1980, and the EHR already has a “Bob Smith” with the same birthday, someone, or something, has to decide whether that’s the same person. Get it wrong, and a documented penicillin allergy doesn’t make it into the chart, with impacts to the med list checked by a nurse, the alert an e-prescribing system doesn’t fire, and the summary an AI tool gives the next clinician. These decisions are made constantly, on multiple platforms, usually in a black box. Trust, But Verify The data layer closest to a patient's identity is where trust is especially important, because every downstream process and technology is built on it. Right now, the trust in that layer largely runs on faith. Open source is a structural advantage here, because it turns that faith into a verifiable process. A company's open source codebase isn't just audited by its employees. Customers, security researchers, and teams building products on top of it can see its judgment calls, spot bugs, and suggest improvements. Third-Party Blind Spots A hospital’s compliance and security teams can review their own systems to see what’s running and how. A proprietary platform used by that hospital, however, isn't scrutinized by anyone besides the vendor that supplies it. PHI breaches involving third-party systems are not uncommon , and when one happens, only the vendor really knows what went wrong or how to fix it. Judgment Calls If a system can't be trusted to identify a patient, it's hard to trust anything built on top of it. When millions of records are involved, there are difficult choices to make, and some mistakes are inevitable. Open source code doesn't build trust with perfect matching, but with transparency: everyone can see how the decisions are made. Broadly speaking, this matching process is straightforward. The devil of course, is in the details. Here's an example of Metriport code that determines whether two very similar records belong to the same person. This example shows some of the decision-making criteria Metriport uses and the judgement call made. Between 0.0 (no information overlap) and 1.0 (virtually identical records), we selected 0.96 as the threshold that determines whether two records are merged into one patient’s history or remain separate. The trade-off between matches and potential errors is public, and we welcome the debate. What Openness Delivers Transparency in action Broader scrutiny provides concrete benefits. Open source codebases receive bug warnings and improvement suggestions from external engineers, and in the spirit of transparency, a company's own developers often work out issues in public. Outliving your vendor From a practical standpoint, open code also offers protection if a vendor changes direction or shuts down. Proprietary code usually disappears along with the company; published code doesn't. Before Facebook shut down its Parse “backend as a service” platform, it open-sourced Parse Server, letting customers migrate their apps onto their own infrastructure. Similarly, after Basho went bankrupt in 2017, its community continued to develop its distributed database and release new features. (In Metriport's case, a company could independently run our open source code, but would face non-code challenges like network agreements.) An open ecosystem Interwoven open source companies tend to be greater than the sum of their parts. Companies that build in the open can plug into each others' work, giving customers more options for interconnected tools versus getting stuck with one vendor. The data layer closest to the patient's identity is the foundation of digital health, making it too critical to trust to a black box. Everything from basic record keeping to AI-assisted diagnosis depends on it, and that dependency deserves to be identifiable. To see what Metriport looks like under the hood, check out our GitHub repository or contact us anytime.
